record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Covering properly edge-colored graphs by rainbow paths
record.original_question: Suppose the edges of an n-vertex graph are properly edge-colored, so no two incident edges share a color. Can the entire edge set always be covered by O(n) rainbow paths, meaning paths that never repeat a color?

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 (Bonamy, Botler, Dross, Naia and Skokan, [1]). Suppose that the edges of an n-vertex graph are coloured in such a way that no two incident edges have the same colour. Can we always cover the edge-set of the graph with O(n) rainbow paths (meaning, paths that do not use the same colour twice)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $c\colon E(G)\to\mathbb{N}$ be a proper edge-coloring of $G$, i.e., any two edges of $G$ that share a vertex receive distinct colors. A path $P$ in $G$ is called rainbow (with respect to $c$) if all edges of $P$ receive pairwise distinct colors. A collection $\mathcal{P}$ of paths in $G$ is said to cover the edge set if every edge of $G$ belongs to at least one path of $\mathcal{P}$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\ge 1$, every $n$-vertex graph $G$, and every proper edge-coloring of $G$, the edge set $E(G)$ can be covered by at most $Cn$ rainbow paths.
artifact.category_tag: Rainbow path covers in edge-colored graphs
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published resolution of this specific question on covering properly edge-colored n-vertex graphs by O(n) rainbow paths. The question is listed among open problems and related work (separating path systems by Bonamy–Botler–Dross–Naia–Skokan, and recent progress on Andersen's conjecture about long rainbow paths) addresses related but distinct questions. No proof or disproof was found.

status_evidence.title: Separating the edges of a graph by a linear number of paths
status_evidence.snippet: Bonamy, Botler, Dross, Naia and Skokan established a linear upper bound for separating path systems, a related question on path covers.
status_evidence.claim: The same authors are active on linear-sized path systems but address a different (separation) problem.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Cycles in Properly Edge-Colored Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies rainbow substructures in properly edge-colored graphs, but does not resolve the O(n) rainbow path cover question.
status_evidence.claim: Related rainbow-structure results do not address covering by O(n) rainbow paths.
